Sheet name: project

You are a construction estimator preparing a quantity take-off. Read THIS plan's keynotes, general notes, detail/section labels, abbreviation key and schedule headers below. List EVERY object a take-off would quantify and, for each, give:
- canonical_name: the STANDARD ESTIMATOR TAKE-OFF ITEM NAME — the term an estimator actually WRITES on a quantity take-off, NOT the plan's raw label or abbreviation. Translate the drawing's own words into the industry-standard take-off item. An estimator reads the plan's abbreviation or note and records the conventional line-item name:
    * "S.C.C.P." / site-cast concrete panel / tilt panel / tilt wall → "Tilt Up Wall"
    * exposed metal roof deck / open-web (bar) joists / no ceiling / roof assembly → "Exposed Structure"
    * sealed or polished slab-on-grade → "Sealed Concrete"
    * hollow-metal door → "Doors-HM"; hollow-metal frame → "Frame-HM"
    * CMU / concrete masonry / block wall → "CMU Wall"
  Use the conventional take-off item name as the canonical name; when the plan uses only an abbreviation, expand it to the standard term.
- aliases: the plan's OWN literal term(s) for it PLUS common synonyms and abbreviations, so a drawing-text lookup still resolves the object (e.g. for "Tilt Up Wall" the aliases carry "S.C.C.P.", "site cast concrete panel", "tilt panel"). ALWAYS put the drawing's own words in aliases.
- basis: HOW it is measured — one of count | linear | wall_area | floor_area | roof_area.
- binding_hint: HOW to recognise it in the drawing geometry — one of: structural_grid_symbol (the repeated symbol on the structural column grid → columns); perimeter_jamb_symbol (a symbol repeating along the perimeter or at door jambs → bollards); exterior_wall / interior_wall (tilt-up / S.C.C.P. panel faces, interior vs exterior); masonry_wall (CMU / block wall); floor_slab; roof_deck; count_from_schedule; or other.
- variant: "interior" or "exterior" where the plan distinguishes the face, else "".
- thickness_in / height_ft: the thickness or height the plan PRINTS for it, copied VERBATIM as text (e.g. "8", "36'-0\""), else "".
Name and classify only — use the industry-standard take-off item name as canonical and put the drawing's own words in aliases. NEVER invent a quantity: do NOT estimate, count or measure — emit no numbers except inside the thickness_in / height_ft text tokens.
